lessonInput.title: Research planning
lessonInput.objectives: Use only the supplied claims to make a defensible distinction without adding outside facts.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: A UX research plan turns a decision need into actionable learning objectives, participants, tasks, evidence-capture roles, and a rehearsal-ready study setup. Claim 1: The team should agree what it wants to learn from the research round before selecting study details. Claim 2: A prototype used in research should work end-to-end and be usable and accessible in the research venue. Claim 3: Researchers should run through test tasks on the day before the research session. Claim 4: A practice session with a team member can expose procedure problems before participants arrive.

claims: A UX research plan turns a decision need into actionable learning objectives, participants, tasks, evidence-capture roles, and a rehearsal-ready study setup.
The team should agree what it wants to learn from the research round before selecting study details.
A prototype used in research should work end-to-end and be usable and accessible in the research venue.
Researchers should run through test tasks on the day before the research session.
A practice session with a team member can expose procedure problems before participants arrive.

anchors.quote: Each round of user research should have clear objectives. Keep your objectives actionable and to the point.
Work with your team to agree what you want to learn from a round of research.
Your prototype or beta service needs to work from end-to-end and be usable and accessible from the research venue.
Run through the test tasks on the day before the research.
To make sure your research goes smoothly, consider running through the session with a team member.

facts: A UX research plan transforms a decision need into actionable learning objectives and study setup.
Team agreement on learning goals must precede the selection of specific study details.
A prototype used in research must function end-to-end and be fully accessible at the venue.
Researchers should run through test tasks on the day before the research session for preparation.
A practice session with a team member can expose procedure problems before participants arrive.

keyTerms.df: A UX research plan converts a decision need into actionable learning objectives and study setup.
keyTerms.eg: Defining participants, tasks, and evidence-capture roles within the research plan.
keyTerms.mi: A research plan is simply a list of things to do during the research session. It does not require defining specific roles or objectives.
keyTerms.cx: A research plan is a blueprint specifying participants, tasks, and roles, not just a simple to-do list.

keyTerms.df: Learning objectives are specific, actionable goals derived from the research plan.
keyTerms.eg: Setting learning objectives based on the research plan before selecting study details.
keyTerms.mi: Learning objectives are vague statements about what the team hopes to discover during the research. They should be broad and open to interpretation.
keyTerms.cx: Learning objectives must be specific and actionable goals derived from the research plan, not vague hopes.

keyTerms.df: A prototype used in research must operate end-to-end and be usable and accessible at the research venue.
keyTerms.eg: Ensuring the prototype works end-to-end and is accessible in the research venue.
keyTerms.mi: A prototype is just a rough sketch or low-fidelity mockup that does not need to be fully functional for research.
keyTerms.cx: A prototype must function end-to-end and be accessible at the venue, meaning it must be fully operational.

scenario.su: A team needs to understand user friction points in a new checkout flow. The actionable problem is determining which specific usability issues to investigate. A real constraint is that the existing prototype must be fully accessible for all participants.
scenario.ma: The team compares the research plan document, the defined learning objectives, and the prototype's end-to-end functionality and accessibility features.

mc.q: When selecting study details, what is the necessary prerequisite before finalizing the specific research study parameters? A team must first agree on what they want to learn from the research round. This agreement precedes the selection of study details.
op: Selecting study details first, then agreeing on learning goals.
Agreeing on learning goals before selecting study details.
Selecting study details first, then defining evidence-capture roles.
Defining evidence-capture roles before agreeing on learning goals.
mc.ex: Team agreement on learning goals must precede the selection of study details, which supports the option agreeing on learning goals before selecting study details, correcting the option selecting study details first, then agreeing on learning goals.

mc.q: A researcher is preparing for a usability test and needs to ensure procedural readiness. What preparation step exposes potential problems before participants arrive? Running through test tasks on the day before the research session exposes procedure problems.
op: Having participants review the research plan beforehand.
Running through test tasks on the day before the research session.
Finalizing the evidence-capture roles with the team.
Ensuring the prototype is fully accessible at the research venue.
mc.ex: Running through test tasks on the day before the research session exposes procedure problems, which supports the option running through test tasks on the day before the research session, correcting the option having participants review the research plan beforehand.

facts: A research plan turns a decision need into actionable learning objectives.
A research plan also sets participant choices, tasks, and evidence-capture roles.
A study setup should be rehearsal-ready before participants enter the room.
The team should agree what it wants to learn before choosing study details.
A practice session with a team member can reveal procedure problems early.

keyTerms.df: A research plan is the structured preparation that converts a decision need into specific study aims and roles.
keyTerms.eg: A team frames a checkout-flow question, then lists participant tasks and who records observations.
keyTerms.mi: A research plan is just a rough agenda for the meeting.
keyTerms.cx: It is broader than an agenda because it organizes what must be learned, not only timing.

keyTerms.df: A study setup is the prepared arrangement of tasks, materials, and room conditions for the session.
keyTerms.eg: The prototype is placed so the participant can complete the path without extra assistance.
keyTerms.mi: A study setup can be assembled after participants arrive.
keyTerms.cx: Preparation must be ready in advance because the session depends on a usable arrangement from the start.

keyTerms.df: A practice session is a rehearsal run that checks whether the procedure works smoothly before the real session.
keyTerms.eg: A team member steps through the tasks while the moderator checks timing and note-taking.
keyTerms.mi: A practice session is useful only after real participants have started the study.
keyTerms.cx: The point is to expose procedure problems beforehand, so rehearsal happens before participants arrive.

scenario.su: A product team has a prototype for an account-reset flow and wants to study it with participants tomorrow. The flow has a missing confirmation screen, and the room plan leaves one observer without a clear note-taking role.
scenario.ma: The draft research plan, the prototype screen sequence, and the note about evidence-capture roles are being compared against the room setup sheet and the task script.

mc.q: A team is choosing between two descriptions: one names learning goals, participant tasks, and note-taking roles; the other mainly lists meeting timing. Which description matches a research plan more closely?
op: The description that only names the prototype screens without study roles.
The description that mainly schedules the meeting blocks and speaker order.
The description that focuses on post-session reporting instead of preparation.
The description that turns a decision need into learning objectives, participants, tasks, and roles.
mc.ex: The research plan is the structure that converts a decision need into learning objectives, participants, tasks, and evidence-capture roles. The timing-only description is closer to a schedule, not a research plan.

mc.q: A moderator notices the prototype fails at the final step, one observer has no note-taking role, and the team has a rehearsal with a colleague before tomorrow. Which action best fits the preparation described?
op: Skip rehearsal and let the participant discover procedure problems first.
Keep the broken end-to-end flow as it is so reactions stay natural.
Start the session and adjust the procedure after the first participant leaves.
Run through the test tasks in a practice session before participants arrive.
mc.ex: A practice session helps expose procedure problems before participants arrive, which fits the rehearsal described. Waiting for the first participant to expose issues would miss the preparation purpose.

claimBoundary: This packet contains anonymous source-bound artifacts only. It contains no provider identity, model identity, route, admission outcome, retry history, compiler receipt, preference, or training authorization.
